heard: NASA assembled a premier planetary explorer from leftover spare parts. Launched in 1989, Magellan was built cheap, but sent on a monumental task. Engineers constructed its main antenna from a voyager spare, saving millions of dollars. Arriving in 1990, it faced a crushing atmosphere and 475 degrees Celsius heat. Thick, opaque clouds blocked all normal optical views of the alien surface. Instead of cameras, Magellan used radar to pierce the deep, toxic haze. Shockingly, this budget spacecraft mapped 98 percent of the volcanic world. In October 1994, engineers commanded it to dive directly into the crushing atmosphere. Its fiery demise destroyed one of NASA's most brilliant recycled creations. You
